assessment.governing_intent: Show, with retained and independently verifiable evidence, that the canonical liveness replacement (monitor_host composition over LivenessProfile, LivenessReconciler and SQLiteOperationalStore) performs correctly on a real, authorized live workload. The required behaviours are dropped-trigger recovery within G+I, suppression of provider/judgment blocks with attributed resolution, duplicate safety under delayed delivery and restart, one-writer ownership, retained attention linkage and exact real outcome readback. The purpose is to satisfy SF-REQ-056-AC-08 before any SWF-29 bootstrap replacement is declared operational. Offline or sandbox success alone does not count.
implementation_unknowns: Step ordering: step 4 is described as 'before or instead of step 3'. The producer must fix a deterministic order, or separate seeded records, so that the suppression, recovery and restart probes do not interfere with one another on the same KnownActive record.

Timing window: G+I is stated as <=360s, while the policy also has confirmation_seconds=90. It must be confirmed whether the gap -> recovery_intent -> readback_confirmed sequence can realistically settle within 360s or whether only detection is bounded, and the probe must be pinned to the design's actual predicate.

Restart race: step 5 needs a SIGTERM delivered after the durable intent exists but before readback settles. The producer needs a reliable way to hit that window on real wall-clock timing, such as observing the store state before signalling.
CLI surface: whether the launch/restart/show subcommands and the fx-b2-supervision.json config shape exist exactly as written or need wiring within the node extent.
Actor identity: whether '--actor factory-director' in the pinned commands is consistent with custody belonging to the IMPLEMENT worker identity, or whether the actor argument must reflect the worker.
Provider/judgment block: whether a FOUNDER_EXCEPTION CorrelatedOutcome adequately represents the 'provider/judgment block' scenario, or whether a provider-block outcome kind must also be exercised.

Verifier reproduction: how the independent verifier reproduces or inspects a real wall-clock, systemd-supervised run from its own worktree, whether by re-execution or by inspecting immutable observation refs.
material_risks: Phase 1 OPERATIONAL evidence against a synthetic record could be misread or misreported as AC-08 closure or as grounds for SWF-29 retirement.
Authority chain: key bindings rest on Founder instructions relayed through an observing session, and the text itself questions whether direct acknowledgment is needed.

The design contract still carries DESIGN_CANDIDATE_WITH_SPECIFY_HOLD. The architecture constraints require applying the pinned contracts, so proceeding on an assumption that WO-220305 superseded the marker may conflict with 'no boundary beyond the pinned design'.
Real wall-clock timing and signal races may make probes 3 and 5 flaky, producing ambiguous PASS/FAIL results and consuming the 3-cycle budget.
Phase 2 against the real factory workload carries real duplicate-effect and one-writer risk on live BIU state. The authorized blast radius is not yet defined.
Using a shared host (ALIENLAPTOP) and systemd --user alongside the live alienintent.service and observer units creates a risk of unit-name or cgroup collision despite the isolated profile root.

Specifically: record the R1-GAP-MONITOR-HOST disposition, define and authorize the exact 'that workload' target for AC-08, state whether the relayed binding needs direct acknowledgment, and decide whether phase 1 should be split out as its own acceptable unit. After those answers are recorded, re-run the Agent Ready assessment on the revised BIU.
owner_clarifications: R1-GAP-MONITOR-HOST: Will SPECIFY or the design owner record a reviewed design revision or disposition that clears the R1-GAP-MONITOR-HOST / DESIGN_CANDIDATE_WITH_SPECIFY_HOLD marker (wave2-design-contracts.md:995) for the monitor_host composition, given that WO-220305 is reported DONE? For example: the live Wave 2 BIU lifecycle records that the bootstrap alienintent-liveness.service currently supervises, a specific named BIU or profile, or something else. Is a live exercise against the real factory state store (not the isolated fx-b2 root) authorized, including its duplicate-effect and blast-radius implications?

Relayed target binding: Does the Director's binding of the fx-b2-liveness-operational target, made under authority relayed through an observing session (ChatGPT), need a separate direct Founder acknowledgment before its evidence can be relied on for any acceptance or retirement decision?

Scope of this BIU versus phase 1: Should this BIU (#125) stay the single unit covering both phases and wait on phase 2 dispositions before DONE? Or does the owner want phase 1 (isolated mechanics proof) carved out as its own accepted unit, with phase 2 re-issued as a separate BIU once the dispositions above exist?
assessment.rationale: The controlling condition is unresolved owner intent in the acceptance predicate. The BIU's own text says DONE requires phase 2, and that phase 2 depends on two owner dispositions (design-marker clearance and Founder interpretation of 'that workload') that have not been made. These are architecture and product-authority questions, not engineering research, so CLARIFY applies rather than READY. SPLIT does not fit because the phase 2 center is not yet executable or independently rejectable: its target and authority are undefined, and SPLIT cannot carry open owner questions. HOLD is not the primary condition because the missing items are owner decisions rather than an unavailable artifact or environment; the reported phase 1 prerequisites (predecessors DONE, target, budget and fixture) are stated as available. Phase 1 appears cohesive and well pinned. If the owner chooses to carve it out as its own unit with mechanics-only acceptance, it would likely assess as READY, with the listed engineering unknowns left to the producer.
assessment.summary: This BIU has two phases. Phase 1 is an isolated supervised exercise of the FX-B2 fixture against a synthetic FX-B2-PROBE record. The text reports that its target, host mechanism, isolated profile root, budget and custody, and fixture steps 1-7 are bound and pinned under relayed Founder authority, and that all five predecessors are DONE. Phase 2 is the SF-REQ-056-AC-08 closure against the real factory workload, and it is the only path to DONE for this BIU. The text states that phase 2 depends on two owner-level dispositions that have not been made: clearance of the R1-GAP-MONITOR-HOST / DESIGN_CANDIDATE_WITH_SPECIFY_HOLD marker, and a Founder interpretation of what 'that workload' means in AC-08, including whether the relayed target binding needs direct acknowledgment. The BIU's own completion predicate therefore rests on unresolved owner intent. Phase 1 is well specified, but on its own it cannot satisfy the acceptance criteria this BIU owns. These are reported facts from the task text and have not been independently verified.
assessment.verification_assessment: Phase 1 acceptance is observable. It has seven pinned probes with explicit expected outcomes (durable liveness events read back from sqlite, refusal codes EFFECT_IDENTITY_USED and HOST_NOT_OWNED/HOST_OUTSIDE_OWNED_UNIT, and verbatim readback) and an OPERATIONAL evidence schema, so one independent verdict on phase 1 mechanics would be meaningful. The BIU's own completion predicate, SF-REQ-056-AC-08, cannot yet be observed or verified. Its target workload is undefined, and it depends on a design marker the text says is still present. A single verdict on the whole BIU is therefore not currently meaningful. Any phase 1 verdict must be labelled as mechanics-only and must not be presented as AC-08 closure.
